label: Brush float itself
summary: The brush float object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way the game uses 'Self' on other types, it lets a GUI line pass this object to another function. The game documents nothing more, and it names no return type for it.

label: Set maximum
summary: Sets the upper limit of a brush float, a number setting of a brush tool.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI never use it, and it takes no arguments in the game's listing, so how the new limit is given is not known.

label: Set minimum
summary: Sets the lower limit of a brush float, a number setting of a brush tool.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI never use it, and it takes no arguments in the game's listing, so how the new limit is given is not known.

label: Set scaled value
summary: Sets the value of a brush float from a scaled number.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it, and it does not say what the scaling is.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The scaled value to set; the game gives no further detail.

label: Set step size
summary: Sets how big one step is when the brush float is changed in steps.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it, and its listing shows no argument.

label: Set value
summary: Sets the current value of a brush float.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it, and its listing shows no argument.

label: Set value from argument
summary: Sets the value of a brush float to the value given to it.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it. Unlike SetValue, it lists one argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The new value; the game gives no further detail.

label: Set from slider
summary: Takes the new value of a brush setting from the slider that was moved.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a brush setting's slider in the engine's map editor changes, and passes the slider itself (`PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`) as the argument.

label: Small step size
summary: The fine step by which a brush setting's slider moves, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the slider step of the amount and hardness settings in the engine's map editor, while the normal step size serves for the mouse wheel there.

label: Step size
summary: The step by which a brush setting changes, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the mouse wheel step of the brush setting sliders in the engine's map editor, and as the slider step of the size setting. The amount and hardness sliders use the small step size for dragging.

label: Value
summary: The current value of a brush setting, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the position of the setting's slider in the engine's map editor (amount, size and hardness).

label: Brush settings access
summary: Gives access to the brush settings object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on to another function as a data context (the object a GUI part works with). The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Brush amount
summary: The amount setting of a map editor brush, as a brush number setting.
details: The game names no return type, but vanilla makes it the data context of the 'Amount' slider, whose minimum, maximum, steps and value then come from it, and shows `Amount.Value` in the box beside it. How strongly the amount applies is not described.

label: Brush diameter
summary: The diameter of a map editor brush, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the edit box beside the brush's 'Size' slider in the engine's map editor.

label: Brush hardness
summary: The hardness setting of a map editor brush, as a brush number setting.
details: The game names no return type, but vanilla makes it the data context of the 'Hardness' slider, whose limits, steps and value then come from it, and shows `Hardness.Value` beside it. Going by its name, it is how hard the brush's edge is; the game does not describe it.

label: Pixel snap
summary: The pixel snapping switch of a map editor brush.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla ticks a check button with `PixelSnap.Get` and flips it with `PixelSnap.Toggle`; that button's tooltip says it toggles pixel snapping of the current brush.

label: Brush radius
summary: The radius setting of a map editor brush, as a brush number setting.
details: The game names no return type, but vanilla makes it the data context of the slider labelled 'Size', whose limits, steps and value then come from it.

label: Brush settings itself
summary: The brush settings object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function, as in 'Building.Self'. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Set brush amount
summary: Takes in a brush amount typed into its edit box in the map editor.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when editing of the box beside the 'Amount' slider is finished; the box hands over its text.

label: Set brush diameter
summary: Takes in a brush diameter typed into its edit box in the map editor.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when editing of the box beside the 'Size' slider is finished; the box hands over its text.

label: Set brush hardness
summary: Takes in a brush hardness typed into its edit box in the map editor.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when editing of the box beside the 'Hardness' slider is finished; the box hands over its text.

label: Brush dropdown access
summary: Gives access to the brush settings dropdown object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Brush diameter
summary: The diameter of the brush whose settings the dropdown holds, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla writes it in yellow on the button of the brush settings dropdown in the engine's map editor (tooltip 'Brush Settings').

label: Brush dropdown itself
summary: The brush settings dropdown object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Brush settings
summary: The brush settings that the dropdown shows and edits.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla makes it the data context of the dropdown's contents in the engine's map editor, so the amount, size, hardness and pixel snap controls inside read from it.

label: Brush thumbnail
summary: The small picture shown for the brush settings dropdown.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla uses it as a texture in the brush settings widget and in the map content editor of the engine's map editor.

label: Open or close dropdown
summary: Opens the brush settings dropdown, or closes it when it is open.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a click in the brush settings widget and in the map content editor of the engine's map editor.

label: Global brush access
summary: Gives access to the global brush settings object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Display amount names
summary: The list of names of the display brush amounts the map editor offers.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla fills a grid of check buttons under the heading 'Display Amount' from it, one per name; each button's tooltip reads 'Click to set the display brush amount' with the name.

label: Display amount active
summary: Whether the named display brush amount is the one switched on in the map editor.
details: Takes the amount's name as text. Vanilla ticks each check button of the 'Display Amount' grid with it, passing the button's own name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the display amount.
fields.values: a text (vanilla passes `CString.GetString`, the name from the list)

label: Global brush itself
summary: The global brush settings object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Set display amount
summary: Switches the map editor's display brush amount to the one named by a text.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a check button of the 'Display Amount' grid is clicked, passing that button's name; the tooltip says it sets the display brush amount.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the display amount to set.
fields.values: a text (vanilla passes `CString.GetString`, the name from the list)

label: Building access
summary: Gives access to the building object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Base cost text
summary: A text describing what the building costs to build, before anything changes the price.
details: Takes a character. Vanilla shows it in the building's encyclopedia entry under the heading 'Base Cost', passing the player (`GetPlayer`). Whose costs the character changes is not shown; going by the name, the text is the base cost.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the text is made for.

label: Description key
summary: A text value shown in vanilla's debug text next to the building's key.
details: Vanilla uses it in a debug text labelled 'key and desc', after the building's key. Going by its name it is the key of the building's description. It is a technical value, not text for players.

label: Description
summary: The building's description text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the building tooltip, where it comes first and the building's effects follow. In the realm window tooltip and the ruined building tooltip of the holding view it comes after the effects.

label: Effect description
summary: A text that lists what the building does for the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it next to the building's description in building tooltips, passing the player. In the tooltip text the description comes first, in the realm window tooltip the effects do.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whose view the effects are listed for; vanilla passes the player.
fields.values: a character, such as the player

label: Effect description here
summary: A text that lists what the building does for a given character in a given province.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tooltip of a ruined building in the holding view, with the viewed character and province.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the effects are shown for.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The province the building stands in.

label: Icon
summary: The building's icon picture.
details: Going by its name. The game does not use it on this type; the same-name lines are other types' icons used as GUI textures. It names no return type.

label: Building illustration
summary: The picture of the building, for a given province.
details: Takes a province. The game names no return type. Vanilla uses it as the texture of a building in the county view, passing the shown province (`Province.Self`), so the picture can differ by place.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The province the picture is for.

label: Key
summary: The building's internal key, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in a debug text that shows the building's key and description key. It is a technical value, not text for players.

label: Building level
summary: The building's level, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the county view and compares levels there: a next building of level 1 gets the word 'Construct', a higher one 'Upgrade to', and a selected building's level is checked against the current one's.

label: Name
summary: The building's name, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as a barony replacing one building with another, and very widely elsewhere. Going by the existence of GetNameNoTooltip, this version probably adds a hover tooltip.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The building's name, without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in titles and visit buttons, for example 'Level I' with the name in the holding view, and in the silk road visit text. Going by its name, it is the version of GetName without a hover tooltip.

label: Rebuild cost text
summary: A text that describes what it costs the given character to rebuild a ruined building.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text of a ruined building in the holding view, after the words 'Cost to Rebuild'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Vanilla passes the viewed character; the game gives no further detail.

label: Building type text
summary: A text describing the building's type.
details: Vanilla shows it in the county view for a building that could be built there (the building of a potential building item). Going by its name, it describes the kind of building rather than its level.

label: Type icon
summary: The icon picture of the building's type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of a map icon, in the map icon layer file. It names no return type.

label: Type name
summary: The name of the building's type, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the 'Ruined' and 'Rebuilding' titles of the holding view, where it appears in parentheses after the building's name, and in a shared tooltip.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the building has an icon.
details: Going by its name only. The game does not use it on this type; the same-name lines check other types (concept tooltips, laws, situation phases) to decide if an icon shows.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the building is valid.
details: Vanilla uses it in the holy site window to decide whether a part is shown. The game does not say what makes a building valid.

label: Building itself
summary: The building itself, handed on as a value to another function.
details: Vanilla uses it in the holy site window: the building is passed to a check whether the holy site's holding has a building from the same chain, which decides the window's text, whether it is enabled and how transparent it is.

label: Building level item access
summary: Gives access to the building level item object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Building
summary: The building that this level item stands for.
details: Going by its name and its return type, a building. The game lists it as a 'Promote' function. The game's same-name lines are about other building lookups.

label: Level icon
summary: The icon picture of the building level item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of a picture in the county view. It names no return type.

label: Level tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the building level item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of an entry in the county view.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether the building level item is the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it in the county view for the 'down' (pressed) state of a button and for the always-transparent setting of a part.

label: On click
summary: What happens when the player clicks the building level item.
details: Vanilla uses it as the click action of entries in the county view. The game does not say what the click does.

label: Level item itself
summary: The building level item itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Activity window access
summary: Gives access to the activity window object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Special progress bar
summary: Gives the named special progress bar of an activity, as a complex bar.
details: Vanilla's activity window files pass the bar's name, such as 'activity_special_type_progression', and use the result as the data context of the progress display. Going by the ActivityWindow name used there.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the bar.

label: Close
summary: Closes the activity window.
details: Going by its name only. The game does not use it on this type; the listed same-name lines are the word 'close' in texts. It returns nothing.

label: Activity
summary: The activity that the window shows.
details: Going by its name. The game's same-name lines use it on a travel plan, not on the window. It names no return type.

label: Background
summary: The background of the activity window.
details: Going by its name and the activity window file, which uses it as ActivityWindow.GetBackground with a texture taken from it. It names no return type.

label: Guest position in subset
summary: A whole number: the position of a character in a named group of guests in the current phase.
details: Going by its name and the scoreboard of the imperial examination, where it is used together with a check whether the player is in the 'entrants' group.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the guest group.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character to look up; the scoreboard passes the player.

label: Characters
summary: A list of characters connected to the activity window.
details: Going by its name only. The game's same-name lines use it on situation participant groups. It names no return type.

label: Guest group
summary: The list of guests of a named group in the activity's current phase.
details: Vanilla texts count the entries to show 'other supporters', 'other detractors' and the remaining contestants, passing a group name such as 'supporter'. Going by the ActivityWindow name used there.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the guest group.

label: Guest group size text
summary: A text that shows how many guests are in a named group of the current phase.
details: Vanilla's coronation window uses it as label text with the group names 'innovator' and 'conservative'. Going by the ActivityWindow name used there.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the guest group.

label: Event window insert
summary: Gives the part of an activity window that is placed inside an event window.
details: Vanilla passes a widget to it and uses the result as the data context of the activity window and the activity locale window. Going by the use there; the game does not describe it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The widget to build the insert for; vanilla passes the widget itself (AccessSelf).

label: Guest sublist
summary: A list of guests picked out by a group name and a phase.
details: Going by its name and the tournament texts, where its result is counted and used to show the winner of a contest. It names no return type, and the argument meaning is a guess from the name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the phase the list is taken from.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Probably the name of the guest group.

label: Guest group names
summary: The list of names of the guest groups that the activity has.
details: Vanilla's tournament contest widget uses it as the list that fills a GUI list. Going by the ActivityLocaleWindow name used there.

label: Intent tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the player's intent in the activity.
details: Vanilla's activity window uses it as a tooltip. Going by its name and the ActivityWindow name used there.

label: Last weekly effect
summary: Data about the last effect that the activity ran in its weekly pulse.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tooltip of a phase in progress under 'Last action', and takes its title. Going by the ActivityWindow name used there.

label: Special progress value
summary: A number: the current value of the activity's special progress.
details: Vanilla's coronation texts show it as the magnificence value, for example out of 25 or 50. Going by the ActivityWindow name used there.

label: Progress segment text
summary: A text that describes one segment of the activity's special progress bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip, passing the segment's position in the list minus a fixed number. Going by the ActivityWindow name used there.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The number of the segment, counted from the list position.

label: Has active event
summary: Whether the activity window has an event that is active right now.
details: Vanilla's activity window uses it, and its negation, to show or hide parts. Going by the ActivityWindow name used there.

label: Is active progress level
summary: Whether the given level of the special progress is the active one.
details: Vanilla uses it with the value of a progress bar item to show or hide the marker of the current level. Going by the ActivityWindow name used there.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The level to check, from a bar item.

label: Is in guest group
summary: Whether a character is in a named guest group of the current phase.
details: Vanilla's imperial examination scoreboard checks whether the player is in the 'entrants' group, for example to show or size a part.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the guest group.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The character to check; vanilla passes the player.

label: Open travel planner
summary: Opens the travel planner from the activity window.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it, and it does not say what the argument is.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

label: Activity window itself
summary: The activity window object itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Sort guest group, all phases
summary: Sets how a guest group is sorted in every phase of the activity.
details: Going by its name and the descending version, which vanilla calls with a group name and the name of a script value that gives the sort order. This one is presumably the ascending order. The game never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the guest group.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The name of the script value used to sort.

label: Sort guest group down, all phases
summary: Sets a guest group to be sorted from highest to lowest in every phase of the activity.
details: Vanilla calls it when a widget starts, for example for the 'charioteers' and the coronation 'supporter' groups, passing the group name and the name of a script value that gives each guest's sort value. Going by the ActivityWindow name used there.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the guest group.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The name of the script value used to sort.

label: Sort guest group
summary: Sets how a guest group is sorted.
details: Going by its name only. It takes three arguments, which the game does not describe. The game never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

label: Sort guest group down
summary: Sets a guest group to be sorted from highest to lowest.
details: Going by its name only. It takes three arguments, which the game does not describe. The game never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

label: Sort guest group now
summary: Sorts a guest group once.
details: Going by its name only. It takes three arguments, which the game does not describe. The game never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

label: Sort guest group down now
summary: Sorts a guest group once, from highest to lowest.
details: Going by its name only. It takes three arguments, which the game does not describe. The game never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

fields.name: Arg2
fields.text: The game gives no detail about this argument.

label: Update guest group
summary: Refreshes the guest group list for a given activity phase.
details: Vanilla's tournament contest widget calls it when the widget starts and when a tab is clicked, passing the planned phase. Going by the ActivityLocaleWindow name used there.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The planned activity phase to refresh the guests for.

label: Language icon access
summary: Gives access to the court language map icon object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Grandest language
summary: The grandest language of the court that the map icon shows.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon layer as the data context of a part of the icon. The game does not say what makes a language the grandest. It names no return type.

label: Native language
summary: The native language of the court that the map icon shows.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon layer as the data context of a part of the icon. It names no return type.

label: Has grandest language
summary: Whether the court language map icon has a grandest language.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon layer to decide whether the part for the grandest language is visible.

label: Has native language
summary: Whether the court language map icon has a native language.
details: Vanilla uses it in the map icon layer to decide whether the part for the native language is visible.

label: Language icon itself
summary: The court language map icon itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Number access
summary: Gives access to the fixed point number object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Fixed point value
summary: The fixed point number itself, as a value.
details: Going by its name only. The game's one same-name line reads a named value ('succession_score') from a list item, which is another type.

label: Number itself
summary: The fixed point number itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Enum value (to change)
summary: The enum value itself, handed to another function that changes something with it.
details: An enum value is one choice from a fixed list. The game names no return type. Vanilla's map content editor passes it on a click to the function that toggles painting a property with that choice.

label: Bundle values mixed
summary: Whether a bundle of enum values holds more than one different value.
details: The game says it is only meant for bundles of enum values. It is not used in vanilla.

label: Dropdown entries
summary: The entries that a dropdown for this enum value offers.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it and names no return type.

label: Dropdown index
summary: A pair of whole numbers that gives the index of the chosen dropdown entry.
details: Going by its name and its return type, a vector of two whole numbers. The game never uses it, and it does not say what the two numbers mean.

label: Value as text
summary: The enum value written as text.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it.

label: Enum value
summary: The enum value itself, handed to another function as an argument.
details: An enum value is one choice from a fixed list. The game names no return type. Vanilla's map content editor passes it to a check of whether property painting is on for that choice, to tick a button.

label: Set dropdown index
summary: Chooses which dropdown entry is selected for the enum value.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it, and its listing shows no argument.

label: Float rectangle access
summary: Gives access to the float rectangle object itself.
details: Going by its name. A float rectangle is an area with decimal corners. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Rectangle
summary: The rectangle itself, as a value.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it and names no return type.

label: Float rectangle itself
summary: The float rectangle itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Key binding access
summary: Gives access to the input binding setting object itself.
details: Going by its name. An input binding is a key or button assigned to an action. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Key binding setting
summary: The key binding setting itself, handed to another function as an argument.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla's settings window passes it, with the binding and a slot number 0 or 1, to the function that opens the popup for setting a key.

label: Integer rectangle access
summary: Gives access to the integer rectangle object itself.
details: Going by its name. An integer rectangle is an area with whole number corners. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Rectangle
summary: The rectangle itself, as a value.
details: Going by its name only. The game never uses it and names no return type.

label: Integer rectangle itself
summary: The integer rectangle itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Commander window access
summary: Gives access to the select commander window object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Can detach commander
summary: Whether the commander can be taken off the army.
details: Vanilla uses it in the army's select commander window to decide whether a button is enabled. The game does not list the conditions.

label: Close
summary: Closes the select commander window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the click action of a close button in the army's select commander window.

label: Detach commander
summary: Takes the commander off the army.
details: Vanilla uses it as the click action of a button in the army's select commander window. It is paired with the check that says whether this is allowed.

label: Army
summary: The army whose commander the window is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in the select commander window as a data context and to show the army's name. It names no return type.

label: List items
summary: The list of entries shown in the select commander window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window's list. The game does not say who the entries are, and names no return type.

label: Commander window itself
summary: The select commander window itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.

label: Text access
summary: Gives access to the text value object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: Text
summary: The text value itself.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a label in the multiplayer game setup, and inside a localize call in the multiplayer types file to turn a key into its text. It names no return type.

label: Text itself
summary: The text value itself, handed on as a value to another function.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact helper window, where the current text entry is passed to the functions that select an asset and check whether it is selected.

label: UTF-8 text access
summary: Gives access to the UTF-8 text value object itself.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses 'AccessSelf' on a widget to pass that widget on as a data context. The game documents nothing more, and names no return type.

label: UTF-8 text
summary: The UTF-8 text value itself.
details: Going by its name only. The game's same-name lines use GetString on dates, which is another type. It names no return type.

label: UTF-8 text itself
summary: The UTF-8 text value itself, handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and the way vanilla uses 'Self' on other types: it passes the current object to another function. The game names no return type for this one.
